newsitem.title: UK: ASDA challenges VAT rules on foodstuffs.
newsitem.headline: ASDA challenges VAT rules on foodstuffs.

text.p: British supermarket group ASDA Group Plc on Tuesday challenged the government to simplify "ridiculous" rules for value added tax (VAT) on foodstuffs, vowing it would sell chocolate Easter Eggs without the levy.

"ASDA is highlighting the ridiculous rules by taking VAT off all Easter Eggs," a statement from the company, whose chairman is standing as a Conservative candidate in the forthcoming UK election, said.
The call comes as the ruling Conservative party is fighting off opposition Labour party claims that the government might introduce VAT on all foodstuffs if reelected.
The Conservatives, trailing Labour in opinion polls, are fielding ASDA's chairman Archie Norman in one of their safest seats, Tunbridge Wells, for the next election.
Norman is credited with turning the ailing ASDA round to profit and carving a niche for the chain by campaigning against retail price controls in areas such as books and over-the-counter medicines.
The supermarket, which prides itself on giving customers cheap prices, said that in general, "essential food items" were sold without VAT while "luxury goods" were not, but said there were anomalies.
While chocolate and Easter Eggs carry VAT, cake covered in chocolate does not while biscuits coated in chocolate are also subject to VAT. Plain biscuits do not carry the tax.
"We think the rules should be simplified so that it's clear when you pay VAT and when you don't," ASDA's buyer for confectionery and snacks Chris Emmel said in a statement.
